title: OSHA: Occupational Safety and Health Administration Standards
overview: This course offers an in-depth understanding of the structure, content, and applicability of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) standards. It covers the identification, avoidance, mitigation, and prevention of safety and health hazards in general industries. The course also emphasizes employers' responsibilities under OSHA and focuses on the effective implementation of safety programs and record-keeping practices.
audience: This course is designed for health and safety directors, field supervisors, engineers, safety professionals, site managers, and anyone looking to deepen their understanding of workplace safety regulations.
methodology: The course will be highly interactive, utilizing group discussions, case studies, and syndicate work. Depending on the participants' roles and industry background, the course content may be tailored to address specific industry needs. Each participant will receive a copy of the OSHA General Industry Regulations handbook for future reference.
competencies: Complying with health and safety regulations
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand and apply the contents of the OSHA 29CFR1910 standards.
Develop an effective safety program that enhances employee morale, boosts productivity, and reduces overall costs.
Identify the training requirements outlined by OSHA standards and determine relevant topics for their organization’s workforce.
Apply OSHA's record-keeping requirements to maintain an accurate workplace injury log.
Differentiate between the rights of workers and the responsibilities of employers as defined by OSHA.
